report:
Short answer
- The evidence supports a concrete difference: the B−A residual difference pushes early-token logits toward vocabulary about professions/credentials, industries, and culinary/restaurant words (e.g., "dissertation", "professional", "Cooking/Restaurant/Chef", "billionaire", "macroeconomic", "technical", "metropolitan").
- This effect is concentrated at the first few token positions in middle-to-late layers, so it would mainly change the model’s next-token probabilities at the start of a sequence (i.e., a topical/style prior), not some late-update reasoning signal.

Why I conclude this
- Localization: the L2 norm is tiny in very early layers and very large in layers ~10–25, with the biggest mass at positions p0–p2 (especially p1). That pattern is typical of a change that affects next-token logit biases / early-sequence priors produced by later-layer residuals.
- Logit-lens tokens: the top tokens pointed to by the difference vectors repeatedly include “dissertation”, “sciences”, “professional/Professional/professionalism”, “Cook/Cooking/restaurant/Restaurant/Chef/kitchen/baking”, “billionaire/macro­­economic”, “technical/Engineering”, and related domain words. These clusters strongly suggest the direction corresponds to professional/academic/industry and culinary topic vocabulary.
- Direction: this is the B minus A vector. Interpreting the logit-lens outputs in that direction implies Model B (relative to A) raises logit-mass on those tokens at the affected positions/layers.

Caveats / uncertainty
- I don’t see behavioral patchscope continuations in the report (no generated continuations printed), so I’m inferring from logit-lens token directions rather than observed sampled completions.
- The signal could reflect several closely related changes (a topical prior toward occupational/food/industry domains, or a change that makes the model prefer nouns/titles/technical terms early). I cannot attribute it to a specific training objective or dataset without more evidence.

Suggested confirmatory checks
- Compare next-token probability differences on a blank/identity prompt for a set of tokens from the clusters (e.g., “dissertation”, “Cooking”, “Professional”, “restaurant”, “billionaire”).
- Generate unconditional/identity-prompt continuations from both checkpoints and measure frequency of professional/culinary tokens in the first few tokens.

If you want, I can propose the exact probe inputs and token lists to run those checks.
